title: Payment Flow (Purchase Bill to Vendor Payment)
context: Finance › Payment Flow (Purchase Bill to Vendor Payment)

cards.title: Seven sequential stages of the supplier payment lifecycle
cards.body:
The supplier payment lifecycle advances through seven sequential commercial operations to clear corporate obligations.
It begins when the accounts department logs the physical supplier invoice on a Document Receipt.
The supplier invoice is officially booked as a Purchase Bill matched against verified warehouse receipts.
Debit notes are raised when price variations, quality rejections, or returned materials require supplier deductions.
Accounts officers generate a Payment Request to approve pending liabilities for payment by due date.
Treasury managers build a Payment Plan to schedule disbursements based on liquidity and payment priority.
A Payment Advice releases approved payments for execution through electronic bank transfers or cheques.
The flow concludes when cashier staff execute the final Payment Voucher updating bank and vendor ledgers.
This structured progression ensures every supplier payment matches delivered goods and approved purchase orders.

cards.title: Roles and segregation of duties throughout payment processing
cards.body:
Processing payments requires strict separation of duties between invoice recording, verification, and disbursement roles.
Receiving clerks log initial supplier invoices to capture physical document arrival dates and vendor numbers.
Accounts officers review delivery quantities, match warehouse receipts, verify rates, and book the purchase bill.
Finance managers review discrepancies, authorize payment requests, and approve debit note deductions.
Treasury officers compile payment plans, evaluate available bank balances, and generate disbursement advice notes.
Disbursing cashiers sign off payment vouchers to complete cash payments or electronic banking dispatches.
This segregation guarantees that no individual can record, approve, and disburse corporate funds independently.
Every stage creates an immutable audit trail connecting the original invoice to the final bank voucher.

cards.title: Three-way matching between order, receipt, and purchase bill
cards.body:
Financial control requires three-way reconciliation before booking supplier liabilities in company accounts.
The Purchase Bill matches invoiced quantities and unit rates against the authorized purchase order.
Billed quantities are validated against accepted delivery quantities recorded on the Material Receipt Note.
Any price escalation above the agreed purchase order rate requires formal commercial management approval.
Unbilled receipt lines can be billed only once, preventing duplicate invoice payments for the same delivery.
This reconciliation guarantees that suppliers are compensated strictly for agreed contractual terms and verified goods.
Discrepancies halt the invoice passing process until purchasing and warehouse teams resolve quantity differences.
Approved bills establish the definitive legal liability recognized in company accounts payable ledgers.

cards.title: Adjusting liabilities using supplier debit notes
cards.body:
Debit notes adjust vendor balances when billing discrepancies, damaged goods, or material returns arise.
If delivered goods fail quality inspection, returned materials are deducted from vendor accounts via debit notes.
Rate differences between supplier invoices and negotiated agreements trigger price adjustment debit notes.
Open debit notes are linked to payment requests to offset amounts owed to the supplier.
This offsetting mechanism prevents overpayment and ensures supplier ledgers reflect true net liabilities.
Debit notes also recalculate input tax credits to ensure statutory goods and services tax compliance.
Treasury officers review open debit notes before approving payment plans to recover company claims.
This reconciliation guarantees that supplier deductions are recovered before cash disbursements leave the company.

cards.title: Liquidity scheduling through payment plans and advice notes
cards.body:
Payment planning coordinates company cash outflows with daily liquidity and working capital limits.
The Payment Plan groups due purchase bills across vendors and ranks them by contractual payment priority.
Treasury managers allocate available bank funds to select bills for immediate settlement by due date.
The finalized plan generates a formal Payment Advice detailing authorized disbursement amounts and payment modes.
The advice instructs the bank or cashier to prepare electronic funds transfers or demand drafts.
Disbursement limits prevent unauthorized payments exceeding designated managerial approval levels.
This staged authorization protects corporate cash reserves and prevents unauthorized treasury disbursements.
Approved advice documents provide definitive instructions for final accounting voucher execution.

cards.title: Disbursement execution and ledger settlement via payment vouchers
cards.body:
The payment flow concludes with the generation and authorization of a formal Payment Voucher.
The voucher credits the designated company bank or cash ledger account and debits the vendor payable account.
Specific invoice references are closed, reducing open accounts payable balances in the General Ledger.
Cheque numbers, electronic transaction references, and payment modes are recorded for audit verification.
This final accounting entry ensures vendor balances and company bank accounts remain fully reconciled.
Bank reconciliation features verify cleared payments against monthly bank statements to identify unpresented cheques.
Authorizing the voucher locks the transaction, completing the procure-to-pay and payment settlement cycle.
Closed invoice references are archived, providing permanent audit lineage from purchase order to bank disbursement.
